entries.name: Maithili
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Mithila region of Bihar in India and in southeastern Nepal.

entries.name: Manipuri
entries.definition: A Tibeto-Burman language of Manipur in northeastern India, also called Meitei.

entries.name: Manx
entries.definition: The Celtic language of the Isle of Man, a Goidelic language closely related to Irish and Scottish Gaelic.

entries.name: Marathi
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken mainly in the Indian state of Maharashtra.

entries.name: Mayan languages
entries.definition: A family of related languages spoken by Maya peoples in Mexico, Guatemala, Belize and Honduras.

entries.name: Media Center Markup Language
entries.definition: An XML-based markup language used to build user interfaces for Windows Media Center applications.

entries.name: Mizo
entries.definition: A Tibeto-Burman language spoken mainly in the Indian state of Mizoram.

entries.name: MXML
entries.definition: An XML-based markup language created by Macromedia, later Adobe, for laying out user interfaces in Flex applications.

entries.name: Ndebele
entries.definition: The name of two related Bantu languages: Northern Ndebele, spoken mainly in Zimbabwe, and Southern Ndebele, spoken in South Africa.

entries.name: Nepali
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language that is the official language of Nepal and is also spoken in parts of India.

entries.name: Objective-C
entries.definition: An object-oriented extension of C used for Apple's macOS and iOS software.

entries.name: Ovambo
entries.definition: A Bantu language, also called Oshiwambo, spoken mainly in northern Namibia and southern Angola.

entries.name: Phoenician
entries.definition: An extinct Canaanite language of the ancient Phoenicians, written in the Phoenician alphabet.

entries.name: PHP
entries.definition: The PHP programming language.

entries.name: PHP 7
entries.definition: Version-specific PHP concept; not all versions of PHP.

entries.name: PL/pgSQL
entries.definition: The procedural language built into PostgreSQL for writing stored functions and triggers.

entries.name: Portuguese
entries.definition: A Romance language spoken in Portugal, Brazil and several other countries.

entries.name: Power Fx
entries.definition: A low-code formula language from Microsoft, modelled on Excel formulas, used in Power Apps and the Power Platform.

entries.name: Prolog
entries.definition: A logic programming language in which programs are written as facts and rules and run by answering queries.

entries.name: Python
entries.definition: Writing programs in Python.

entries.name: Quechua
entries.definition: A family of Indigenous languages spoken in the Andes of South America, of which Southern Quechua has the most speakers.

entries.name: Romanian
entries.definition: A Romance language spoken mainly in Romania and Moldova.

entries.name: Sakha
entries.definition: A Turkic language spoken mainly in the Sakha Republic in the Russian Far East.

entries.name: Sango
entries.definition: A language of the Central African Republic, used as a lingua franca and an official language alongside French.

entries.name: Santali
entries.definition: An Austroasiatic language spoken by the Santal people of eastern India, Bangladesh and Nepal.

entries.name: Saraiki
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken mainly in the south of Punjab province in Pakistan.

entries.name: SAS macro language
entries.definition: The text-substitution language in SAS that generates and controls SAS code through macro variables and macros.

entries.name: Sass
entries.definition: A stylesheet language that extends CSS with variables, nesting and mixins and is compiled into ordinary CSS.

entries.name: Scala
entries.definition: Writing programs in Scala.

entries.name: Service Provisioning Markup Language
entries.definition: An OASIS XML-based standard for exchanging user, resource and service provisioning information between systems.

entries.name: Shan
entries.definition: A Tai language spoken by the Shan people, mainly in Shan State, Myanmar.

entries.name: Silesian
entries.definition: A West Slavic language spoken in Upper Silesia, mainly in southern Poland.

entries.name: Slovene
entries.definition: A South Slavic language spoken mainly in Slovenia.

entries.name: Sogdian
entries.definition: An extinct Eastern Iranian language that served as a trade language along the Silk Road.

entries.name: SQL
entries.definition: Expressing database queries and data operations in SQL.

entries.name: Swift
entries.definition: The Swift programming language; the bare label is context-sensitive.

entries.name: TypeScript
entries.definition: Writing typed JavaScript programs with TypeScript.

entries.name: UML
entries.definition: A language for modeling software systems.

entries.name: XBRL
entries.definition: An XML-based standard language for tagging and exchanging business and financial reporting data.

entries.name: XML
entries.definition: A markup language for structured documents.
